newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Troops take up positions in Armenian capital.
newsitem.headline: Troops take up positions in Armenian capital.

text.p: Elite commando troops took up positions around key buildings in the Armenian capital Yerevan on Tuesday as the country appeared bound for an acute political crisis over Sunday's presidential election.

More than 100 red-beret clad soldiers fanned out around the large brick parliament building and security was beefed up at the official residence of President Levon Ter-Petrosyan, who has claimed victory but whom the main contender accused of massive election fraud.
The troops said they had been brought there in expectation of a large rally in support of former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan who opposed Ter-Petrosyan in the first post-Soviet election.

Manukyan led 50,000 peaceful protesters throught the streets of central Yerevan on Monday after first election returns indicated that Ter-Petrosyan was winning. Manukyan said the government had rigged the vote in favor of Ter-Petrosyan.
The official results of the polls have not been announced yet.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which has been coordinating 89 international observers, issued a preliminary report criticising "very serious" irregularities in voting procedures.
